newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures reverse gains to end lower.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures reverse gains to end lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly lower after Standard & Poor's 500s reversed gains in fast trade on expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates by the end of the year, traders said.
The economic advisory committee of the PSA The Bond Market Trade Association said late Wednesday that positive U.S economic growth through 1997 should prompt a Fed rate hike.
The committee projected the Federal funds rate would rise to 6.0 percent from 5.50 percent by the end of 1997.
The statement, coupled with talk that a hedge fund sold $1 billion of cash 10-year T-notes, pushed T-bond prices lower.
The yield on the 30-year cash T-bond rose to 6.74 percent, and led to concerns that U.S. investors may shift assets into U.S. government securities from U.S. stocks, traders said.

September S&Ps spiked down to the initial 15-point daily limit to 890.00 as soon as T-bond futures closed. One U.S. dealer was a buyer of S&Ps, boosting September off the limit and preventing a two-minute trading halt, traders said.

A trading halt occurs if the lead S&P contract remains locked at the limit after 15 minutes or until 1430 CDT/1930 GMT. The next downside limit for S&P futures would have been 30 points until 1430 CDT/1930 GMT.
Earlier in the day, September S&Ps rose nearly to the all-time high of 912.40, and end-of-quarter buying was expected to lift the contract to 920.00 by the end of the week, traders said.
"Going into the end of the second quarter there will be a big mark-up for a lot of these mutual funds," one S&P futures trader said.

"And it really helped these managers that the market sold off sharply on Monday," he said. September S&Ps fell more than 20 points on Monday, but then rebounded about 24 points on Tuesday above the all-time settlement high of 907.50.
Traders have attributed the market's string of record highs since June 6 to waning expectations that the U.S. Fed will raise rates at its next policy-making meeting on July 1-2.
Speculation had also been mounting, given recent tame consumer and producer prices, that U.S. economic growth might slow in the third quarter.
The PSA's annual mid-year economic forecast dampened that speculation.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin also said U.S. economic conditions were "very good" and were likely to remain good.
Rubin also told reporteres that while there was no reason to expect concerted selling of U.S. Treasuries, U.S. financial markets were big enough to absorb such selling if it were to occur.
Arbitrage buy and sell programs were noted before the sell-off, with buy programs at a 9.80-point premium and sells at a 7.80 premium. Fair value stood at 8.62 points to cash.

At the end of pit trade, Sept S&Ps were off 8.75 at 896.25, KCBT Value Lines were down 7.00 at 788.50, NYSE Composites were down 3.80 at 467.00, Nikkeis were up 345 at 20,775, Midcap 400s were off 2.40 at 289.40, Nasdaq 100s fell 10.75 to 989.00 and Russell 2000s lost 3.35 to 394.90. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
